mechanism_narrative: The steep recent rebound in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS signals broader local footfall recovery that spills into discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC will rise over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:both series turned positive by t-1w and stayed elevated at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS remain positive while RETAIL_REC does not improve versus the prior 4 weeks, the spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains depressed but stops falling and WORKPLACES stabilizes, accumulated commuting normalization translates into more retail trips with a one-week lag, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week after being below -20
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -39.1 to -14.0 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above the stated threshold but RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week, the commuting-to-retail lag claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: A broad reopening regime in which WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain less negative than four weeks earlier will continue to pull retail activity upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved monotonically from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue to recover but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days, the reopening transmission is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An upward PARKS shock indicates warmer or more favorable outdoor conditions that also raise destination shopping, so RETAIL_REC will move up over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -10.6 at t-3w to 16.3 at t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS turns positive but RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks, the weather/outdoor-footfall linkage is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates continued suppression of city-center trips, which should keep RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week average over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:both remain far below baseline despite recent improvement
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay depressed but RETAIL_REC rises above the previous 4-week mean, the suppression mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in RESIDENTIAL and fall in TRANSIT means more time spent near home and fewer discretionary downtown trips, so retail-and-recreation mobility will decline within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +2 while TRANSIT remains below -15
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive while TRANSIT stayed negative in all four weeks
failure_condition: If the home-centered pattern persists yet RETAIL_REC does not weaken within two weeks, the substitution-away-from-retail mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If grocery and pharmacy visits stay positive while transit remains muted, essential errand consolidation will crowd out discretionary shopping trips, keeping RETAIL_REC from recovering over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 0 while TRANSIT stays below -10
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM turned positive at t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains positive and TRANSIT stays depressed but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the crowding-out claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: The recent jump in PARKS followed by a slight pullback implies the outdoor-season impulse has already peaked, so retail-and-recreation mobility will soften relative to the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose to 16.3 at t-1w then eased to 11.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS cools after a spike but RETAIL_REC does not weaken in the next week, the peak-outdoor-season hypothesis is rejected.
